stem: A neighboring pollen-producing field is farther away than a source used in a previous season, but it is much larger and prevailing winds differ. What is the strongest risk interpretation?
choices: Reassess pollen risk from source size, distance, wind and crop consequence rather than treating one isolation distance as a guarantee
Assume greater distance always means zero risk
Ignore source size because only distance matters
Use property lines as the pollen boundary
rationale: Pollen deposition generally declines with distance but source strength and weather affect the long-tail risk, so isolation is risk reduction rather than a zero-risk guarantee.
